{{神社 |名称 = 六所神社 |画像 = [[ファイル:六所神社 (市川市) 正面.JPG|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田2丁目22 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|44|11.73|N|139|55|01.30|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=六所神社}} |祭神 = [[大国主|大己貴尊]]
[[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]]
[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]
[[大宮売神|大宮売尊]]
[[布留御魂|布留之御魂]]
[[ニニギ|彦火瓊々杵尊]] |神体 = |社格 = [[下総国]][[総社]]
旧[[村社]] |創建 = |本殿 = |別名 = 六所宮 |札所等 = |例祭 = [[10月20日]] |神事 = }} {{座標一覧}} [[ファイル:六所神社 (市川市) 鳥居.JPG|thumb|200px|right|鳥居]] '''六所神社'''（ろくしょじんじゃ）は、[[千葉県]][[市川市]]にある[[神社]]。[[下総国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[村社]]。 == 概要 == [[古代]]、[[国司]]は各国内の全ての神社を一宮から順に巡拝していた。これを効率化するため、各国の[[国府]]近くに国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]を設け、まとめて祭祀を行うようになった。当社はそのうちの[[下総国]]の総社にあたる。 現在地に遷座するまでは、国府台のスポーツセンターの位置に鎮座していた。社伝では12代[[景行天皇]]の勅願によるという境内説明板。。国府台一帯は下総国府の推定地とされており、発掘調査も度々行われている。遷座は明治19年に陸軍練兵場造成のために行われたが、当地が選ばれたのは神主の屋敷地があった関係とされる『千葉県の地名』須和田村項。。 == 祭神 == 祭神は以下の6柱祭神は境内説明板に従って表記。。 * [[大国主|大己貴尊]] （おおなむちのみこと） * [[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]] （いざなぎのみこと） * [[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]] （すさのうのみこと） * [[大宮売神|大宮売尊]] （おおみやめのみこと） * [[布留御魂|布留之御魂]] （ふるのみたま） * [[ニニギ|彦火瓊々杵尊]] （ひこほににぎのみこと） == 境内 == ファイル:六所神社 (市川市) 本殿.JPG|本殿 ファイル:六所神社 (市川市) 拝殿.JPG|拝殿 == 関係地 == [[ファイル:下総総社跡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|下総総社跡（市川市国府台）]] * 下総総社跡（市川市国府台、{{ウィキ座標|35|44|38.48|N|139|54|26.77|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|位置|name=下総総社跡（旧鎮座地）}}） :: 現在のスポーツセンターの位置にある当社旧鎮座地。一帯は大樹が多く「六所の森」の名があり、神社跡から南の地は「府中」と呼ばれていた[http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html 下総総社跡]（市川市ホームページ）。 。当地からは平安時代初期までの竪穴住居の遺構が見つかっていることから、それ以後に総社が設けられたと見られている。跡地は現在「下総総社跡」として市川市の史跡に指定されている。 == 祭事 == * 元旦祭 （[[1月1日]]）祭事の一覧は境内説明板よる。 * 節分祭 （2月） * 祈年祭 （[[2月17日]]） * 大祓式 （[[6月30日]]） * 大祭 （[[10月20日]]） * 勤労感謝祭 （[[11月23日]]） * 七五三才祝 （11月15日前の日曜日） * 大祓式 （[[12月31日]]） == 文化財 == === 下野市指定文化財 === * 下総総社跡（史跡） - スポーツセンター付近の旧社地 == 現地情報 == ; 所在地 * [[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田2丁目22 ; 交通アクセス * 最寄駅：[[京成電鉄]][[京成本線]] [[市川真間駅]] （徒歩約11分） * [[東日本旅客鉄道|JR東日本]][[総武本線]] [[市川駅]] （徒歩約18分） ; 周辺 * [[下総国分寺]] == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * 『日本歴史地名体系 千葉県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）市川市 下総国府跡項・須和田村項 == 外部リンク == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html 下総総社跡]（市川市ホームページ） * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 六所神社]（神社のひろば -千葉県神社庁監修-） {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ろくしよしんしやいちかわし}} [[category:千葉県の神社]] [[Category:市川市]] [[Category:総社]] [[category:千葉県の旧村社]] [[Category:下総国|社ろくしよしんしや]]

昭和50年1月8日指定[http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1551000006.html 文化財（市指定）]（市川市ホームページ）。。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田2丁目22 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道 ** [[京成電鉄]][[京成本線]] [[市川真間駅]] （徒歩約11分） ** [[東日本旅客鉄道]]（JR東日本）[[総武本線]] [[市川駅]] （徒歩約18分） '''周辺''' * [[下総国分寺]] == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1996|chapter=|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 12 千葉県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490121|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「下総国府跡」|ref={{Harvid|下総国府跡（平凡社）|1996年}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「須和田村」|ref={{Harvid|須和田村（平凡社）|1996年}}}}。 == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)}} * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html 下総総社跡] - revision.text:
{{Infobox Shrine | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | address = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deities = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== Annual Festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s Festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun Festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae Ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand Festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving Festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Shimōsa Sōja Ruins**: Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.

'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.

{{Infobox Shrine | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | address = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deities = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== Annual Festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s Festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun Festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae Ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand Festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving Festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Shimōsa Sōja Ruins**: Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * **Location**: Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * **By Train**: * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Shimōsa Sōja Ruins**: Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * **location**: Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * **By Train**: * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Shimōsa Sōja Ruins**: Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * **location**: Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * **By Train**: * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Shimōsa Sōja Ruins**: Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * **location**: Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * **By Train**: * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Shimōsa Sōja Ruins**: Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * **location**: Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * **By Train**: * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Shimōsa Sōja Ruins**: Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * **location**: Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * **By Train**: * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': * 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. * 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19年}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
