{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year }} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year }} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year }} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
{{Shinto-stub}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year }} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year }} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日|12=draft}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市|12=draft}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司|12=draft}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year|12=draft}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=draft}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線|12=draft}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線|12=draft}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺|12=draft}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日|12=draft}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市|12=draft}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司|12=draft}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year|12=draft}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=draft}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線|12=draft}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線|12=draft}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺|12=draft}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市|12=draft}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司|12=draft}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year|12=draft}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=draft}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線|12=draft}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線|12=draft}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺|12=draft}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日|12=draft}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市|12=draft}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司|12=draft}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year|12=draft}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=draft}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線|12=draft}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線|12=draft}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺|12=draft}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日|12=draft}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市|12=draft}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司|12=draft}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year|12=draft}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=draft}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線|12=draft}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線|12=draft}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺|12=draft}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px|thumb|Haiden of Rokusho Shrine]] | coordinates = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|ja|10月20日|12=draft}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in {{ill|Ichikawa|ja|市川市|12=draft}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Provincial Governor|ja|国司|12=draft}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|12=draft}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|ja|明治19th year|12=draft}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=draft}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=draft}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=draft}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=draft}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa-Mama Station|ja|市川真間駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|ja|京成本線|12=draft}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|ja|市川駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|ja|総武本線|12=draft}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubunji|ja|下総国分寺|12=draft}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{神社 |名称 = 六所神社 |画像 = [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg|250px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田2丁目22-7 |位置 = {{WikidataCoord|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[大国主|大己貴尊]]
[[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]]
[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]
[[大宮売神|大宮売尊]]
布留之御魂
[[ニニギ|彦火瓊々杵尊]] |神体 = |社格 = [[下総国]][[総社]]
旧[[村社]] |創建 = |本殿 = |別名 = 六所宮 |札所等 = |例祭 = [[10月20日]] |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Chiba|label=六所神社|float=center|relief=1|caption=|width=200}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200}} }} {{座標一覧}} [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|鳥居}}]] [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿}}]] '''六所神社'''（ろくしょじんじゃ）は、[[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田にある[[神社]]。[[下総国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[村社]]。 == 概要 == [[古代]]、[[国司]]は各国内の全ての神社を一宮から順に巡拝していた。これを効率化するため、各国の[[国府]]近くに国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]を設け、まとめて祭祀を行うようになった。当社はそのうちの[[下総国]]の総社に比定される。 この六所神社は、現在地に遷座するまでは国府台のスポーツセンターの位置に鎮座した。社伝では12代[[景行天皇]]の勅願による創建という境内説明板。。国府台一帯は下総国府の推定地とされており、発掘調査も度々行われている。遷座は[[1886年]]（[[明治]]19年）の陸軍練兵場造成に伴うものであったが、現在地が選ばれたのは神主の屋敷地があった関係とされる{{Sfn|須和田村（平凡社）|1996年}}。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の6柱。 * [[大国主|大己貴尊]]（おおなむちのみこと） * [[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]]（いざなぎのみこと） * [[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]（すさのうのみこと） * [[大宮売神|大宮売尊]]（おおみやめのみこと） * 布留之御魂（ふるのみたま） * [[ニニギ|彦火瓊々杵尊]]（ひこほににぎのみこと） == 祭事 == 六所神社で年間に行われる祭事の一覧。 * 元旦祭 （[[1月1日]]） * 節分祭 （2月） * 祈年祭 （[[2月17日]]） * 大祓式 （[[6月30日]]） * 大祭 （[[10月20日]]） * 勤労感謝祭 （[[11月23日]]） * 七五三才祝 （11月15日前の日曜日） * 大祓式 （[[12月31日]]） == 関係地 == [[File:Shimosa-soja-ato, sekihi.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|下総総社跡（市川市国府台）}}{{small|市川市指定史跡。}}]] * 下総総社跡（市川市[[国府台 (市川市)|国府台]]、{{ウィキ座標|35|44|38.48|N|139|54|26.77|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|位置|name=下総総社跡（旧鎮座地）}}） *: 現在の市川市スポーツセンターの位置にある六所神社旧鎮座地。一帯は大樹が多く「六所の森」の名があり、神社跡から南の地は「府中」と呼ばれていた[http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html 下総総社跡]（市川市ホームページ）。 。当地では平安時代初期までの[[竪穴建物]]の遺構が見つかっており、それ以後に総社が設けられたと見られている。この旧鎮座地は、現在では「下総総社跡」として市川市指定史跡に指定されている。 == 文化財 == === 市川市指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 下総総社跡 - 1975年（昭和50年）1月8日指定[http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1551000006.html 文化財（市指定）]（市川市ホームページ）。。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田2丁目22 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道 ** [[京成電鉄]][[京成本線]] [[市川真間駅]] （徒歩約11分） ** [[東日本旅客鉄道]]（JR東日本）[[総武本線]] [[市川駅]] （徒歩約18分） '''周辺''' * [[下総国分寺]] == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1996|chapter=|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 12 千葉県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490121|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「下総国府跡」|ref={{Harvid|下総国府跡（平凡社）|1996年}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「須和田村」|ref={{Harvid|須和田村（平凡社）|1996年}}}}。 == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)}} * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html 下総総社跡] - 市川市ホームページ * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 六所神社] - 千葉県神社庁監修「神社のひろば」 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ろくしよしんしや いちかわし}} [[category:千葉県の神社]] [[Category:市川市の建築物]] [[Category:市川市の歴史]] [[Category:総社]] [[category:千葉県の旧村社]] [[Category:下総国|社0]]

旧[[村社]] |創建 = |本殿 = |別名 = 六所宮 |札所等 = |例祭 = [[10月20日]] |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Chiba|label=六所神社|float=center|relief=1|caption=|width=200}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200}} }} {{座標一覧}} [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|鳥居}}]] [[File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿}}]] '''六所神社'''（ろくしょじんじゃ）は、[[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田にある[[神社]]。[[下総国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[村社]]。 == 概要 == [[古代]]、[[国司]]は各国内の全ての神社を一宮から順に巡拝していた。これを効率化するため、各国の[[国府]]近くに国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]を設け、まとめて祭祀を行うようになった。当社はそのうちの[[下総国]]の総社に比定される。 この六所神社は、現在地に遷座するまでは国府台のスポーツセンターの位置に鎮座した。社伝では12代[[景行天皇]]の勅願による創建という境内説明板。。国府台一帯は下総国府の推定地とされており、発掘調査も度々行われている。遷座は[[1886年]]（[[明治]]19年）の陸軍練兵場造成に伴うものであったが、現在地が選ばれたのは神主の屋敷地があった関係とされる{{Sfn|須和田村（平凡社）|1996年}}。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の6柱。 * [[大国主|大己貴尊]]（おおなむちのみこと） * [[イザナギ|伊弉諾尊]]（いざなぎのみこと） * [[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]（すさのうのみこと） * [[大宮売神|大宮売尊]]（おおみやめのみこと） * 布留之御魂（ふるのみたま） * [[ニニギ|彦火瓊々杵尊]]（ひこほににぎのみこと） == 祭事 == 六所神社で年間に行われる祭事の一覧。 * 元旦祭 （[[1月1日]]） * 節分祭 （2月） * 祈年祭 （[[2月17日]]） * 大祓式 （[[6月30日]]） * 大祭 （[[10月20日]]） * 勤労感謝祭 （[[11月23日]]） * 七五三才祝 （11月15日前の日曜日） * 大祓式 （[[12月31日]]） == 関係地 == [[File:Shimosa-soja-ato, sekihi.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|下総総社跡（市川市国府台）}}{{small|市川市指定史跡。}}]] * 下総総社跡（市川市[[国府台 (市川市)|国府台]]、{{ウィキ座標|35|44|38.48|N|139|54|26.77|E|region:JP-12_type:landmark|位置|name=下総総社跡（旧鎮座地）}}） *: 現在の市川市スポーツセンターの位置にある六所神社旧鎮座地。一帯は大樹が多く「六所の森」の名があり、神社跡から南の地は「府中」と呼ばれていた[http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html 下総総社跡]（市川市ホームページ）。 。当地では平安時代初期までの[[竪穴建物]]の遺構が見つかっており、それ以後に総社が設けられたと見られている。この旧鎮座地は、現在では「下総総社跡」として市川市指定史跡に指定されている。 == 文化財 == === 市川市指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 下総総社跡 - 1975年（昭和50年）1月8日指定[http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1551000006.html 文化財（市指定）]（市川市ホームページ）。。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[千葉県]][[市川市]]須和田2丁目22 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道 ** [[京成電鉄]][[京成本線]] [[市川真間駅]] （徒歩約11分） ** [[東日本旅客鉄道]]（JR東日本）[[総武本線]] [[市川駅]] （徒歩約18分） '''周辺''' * [[下総国分寺]] == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1996|chapter=|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 12 千葉県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490121|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「下総国府跡」|ref={{Harvid|下総国府跡（平凡社）|1996年}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「須和田村」|ref={{Harvid|須和田村（平凡社）|1996年}}}}。 == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)}} * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html 下総総社跡] - 市川市ホームページ * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 六所神社] - 千葉県神社庁監修「神社のひろば」 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ろくしよしんしや いちかわし}} [[category:千葉県の神社]] [[Category:市川市の建築物]] [[Category:市川市の歴史]] [[Category:総社]] [[category:千葉県の旧村社]] [[Category:下総国|社0]]

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q17220798]] Wikidata name: Rokusho-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:57, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = [[:en:October 20|October 20]] | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|qid=Q209785}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichikawa, Chiba|Ichikawa]], Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:Kokushi (official)|Provincial Governor]] would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]].
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in [[:en:1886|Meiji 19]] due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawamama Station|Ichikawa-Mama Station]] on the [[:en:Keisei Main Line|Keisei Main Line]]. ** 18-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawa Station|Ichikawa Station]] on the [[:en:Sōbu Main Line|Sōbu Main Line]].
== Nearby Sites == * [[:en:Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|Shimōsa Kokubunji]] – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q17220798]] Wikidata name: Rokusho-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:57, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = [[:en:October 20|October 20]] | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|qid=Q209785}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichikawa, Chiba|Ichikawa]], Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:Kokushi (official)|Provincial Governor]] would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]].
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in [[:en:1886|Meiji 19]] due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawamama Station|Ichikawa-Mama Station]] on the [[:en:Keisei Main Line|Keisei Main Line]]. ** 18-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawa Station|Ichikawa Station]] on the [[:en:Sōbu Main Line|Sōbu Main Line]].
== Nearby Sites == * [[:en:Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|Shimōsa Kokubunji]] – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q17220798]] Wikidata name: Rokusho-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:57, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = [[:en:October 20|October 20]] | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichikawa, Chiba|Ichikawa]], Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:Kokushi (official)|Provincial Governor]] would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]].
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in [[:en:1886|Meiji 19]] due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawamama Station|Ichikawa-Mama Station]] on the [[:en:Keisei Main Line|Keisei Main Line]]. ** 18-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawa Station|Ichikawa Station]] on the [[:en:Sōbu Main Line|Sōbu Main Line]].
== Nearby Sites == * [[:en:Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|Shimōsa Kokubunji]] – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]].
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in [[:en:1886|Meiji 19]] due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawamama Station|Ichikawa-Mama Station]] on the [[:en:Keisei Main Line|Keisei Main Line]]. ** 18-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawa Station|Ichikawa Station]] on the [[:en:Sōbu Main Line|Sōbu Main Line]].
== Nearby Sites == * [[:en:Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|Shimōsa Kokubunji]] – A historical Buddhist temple site.

'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichikawa, Chiba|Ichikawa]], Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:Kokushi (official)|Provincial Governor]] would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]].
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in [[:en:1886|Meiji 19]] due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawamama Station|Ichikawa-Mama Station]] on the [[:en:Keisei Main Line|Keisei Main Line]]. ** 18-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawa Station|Ichikawa Station]] on the [[:en:Sōbu Main Line|Sōbu Main Line]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q17220798]] Wikidata name: Rokusho-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:57, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = [[:en:October 20|October 20]] | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichikawa, Chiba|Ichikawa]], Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:Kokushi (official)|Provincial Governor]] would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]].
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in [[:en:1886|Meiji 19]] due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawamama Station|Ichikawa-Mama Station]] on the [[:en:Keisei Main Line|Keisei Main Line]]. ** 18-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawa Station|Ichikawa Station]] on the [[:en:Sōbu Main Line|Sōbu Main Line]].
== Nearby Sites == * [[:en:Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|Shimōsa Kokubunji]] – A historical Buddhist temple site.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q17220798]] Wikidata name: Rokusho-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:57, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = [[:en:October 20|October 20]] | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Ichikawa, Chiba|Ichikawa]], Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]] and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, [[:en:Kokushi (official)|Provincial Governor]] would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of [[:en:Shimōsa Province|Shimōsa Province]].
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in [[:en:1886|Meiji 19]] due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]].
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawamama Station|Ichikawa-Mama Station]] on the [[:en:Keisei Main Line|Keisei Main Line]]. ** 18-minute walk from [[:en:Ichikawa Station|Ichikawa Station]] on the [[:en:Sōbu Main Line|Sōbu Main Line]].
== Nearby Sites == * [[:en:Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|Shimōsa Kokubunji]] – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
