<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]]
{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}

Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20|1=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20|1=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[Category:sn_crud|TESTcommons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]]
{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20|1=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20|1=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[Category:sn_crud|TESTcommons:Category:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa)]][[ja:六所神社 (市川市)]]
{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20|1=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20|1=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Rokusho Shrine | image = File:Rokusho-jinja (Ichikawa), Haiden.jpg | coordinates = {{Coord|35.73661111111111|N|139.91702777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | location = Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture, Japan | deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}} | established = Unknown (traditional date during the reign of Emperor Keikō) | festivals = {{ill|October 20|en|October 20|WD=Q2959|lt=October 20|1=October 20}} | location = {{ill|Ichikawa|WD=Q209785|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}} }}
'''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{nihongo|六所神社|ろくしょじんじゃ}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ichikawa, Chiba|en|Ichikawa, Chiba|WD=Q209785|lt=Ichikawa|1=Ichikawa, Chiba}}, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Historically, it served as the {{nihongo|Sōja|総社}} (provincial general shrine) of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}} and was classified as a [[village shrine]] ({{nihongo|sonsha|村社}}) under the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].
== Overview == In ancient Japan, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|WD=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor|1=Kokushi (official)}} would visit all the shrines in their province in order of importance. To streamline this practice, a single "general shrine" was established near the provincial capital, where the province’s deities were enshrined collectively. Rokusho Shrine is regarded as the Sōja of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|WD=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province|1=Shimōsa Province}}.
Originally located at the site of present-day Ichikawa City Sports Center, the shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1886|en|1886|WD=Q7822|lt=Meiji 19|1=1886}} due to the construction of a military training ground. The new site was chosen because it was the residence of the shrine's priest.
== Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines six deities: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) * {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イザナギ}} * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}} * {{ill|Ōmiyame-no-Kami|ja|大宮売神|1=Ōmiya-no-Me|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiyame-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya-no-Me|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} * Furu no Mitama * {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}}
== festivals == The following festivals are held annually at the shrine: * New Year’s festival ({{nihongo|Gantan-sai|元旦祭}}) – January 1 * {{nihongo|Setsubun festival|節分祭}} – February * {{nihongo|Kinensai|祈年祭}} – February 17 * {{nihongo|Ōharae ceremony|大祓式}} – June 30 and December 31 * Grand festival ({{nihongo|Taisai|大祭}}) – October 20 * Labor Thanksgiving festival ({{nihongo|Kinrō Kansha-sai|勤労感謝祭}}) – November 23 * {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三才祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichi-Go-San|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Sunday before November 15
== Historical Significance == The shrine was traditionally located at {{nihongo|Shimōsa Sōja Ruins|下総総社跡}}, believed to be the site of the provincial capital of Shimōsa. Excavations in the area have uncovered remains of pit dwellings from the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, suggesting that the site served as the Sōja from that time.
The current location was selected after the shrine’s relocation in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.
== Cultural Properties == === Ichikawa City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Shimōsa Sōja Ruins''': Designated as a historic site by Ichikawa City in 1975.
== Access == * '''location''': Suwada 2-22-7, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. * '''By Train''': ** 11-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawamama Station|en|Ichikawamama Station|WD=Q5986159|lt=Ichikawa-Mama Station|1=Ichikawamama Station}} on the {{ill|Keisei Main Line|en|Keisei Main Line|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}. ** 18-minute walk from {{ill|Ichikawa Station|en|Ichikawa Station|WD=Q1067608|lt=Ichikawa Station|1=Ichikawa Station}} on the {{ill|Sōbu Main Line|en|Sōbu Main Line|WD=Q1191364|lt=Sōbu Main Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}.
== Nearby Sites == * {{ill|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|en|Shimōsa Kokubun-ji|WD=Q17128370|lt=Shimōsa Kokubunji|1=Shimōsa Kokubun-ji}} – A historical Buddhist temple site.
== References == {{reflist}}
== External Links == * [http://www.city.ichikawa.lg.jp/edu09/1521000012.html Shimōsa Sōja Ruins] – Official site (Ichikawa City) * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=3019 Rokusho Shrine] – Chiba Prefecture Shrine Association
